quoted_clause.quote: This Rate Schedule is for large general service supplied from available lines of 69,000 volts or higher to large load (data center) customers that commenced service on or after October 1, 2025, and have a peak electric demand of 50 MW or greater at a single facility or at least equal to 75 MW in the aggregate among facilities taking service from PPL Electric at or above 69 kV within a 10-mile radius

threshold_mw.value: 50 MW or more peak demand at a single facility, or at least 75 MW in the aggregate among the customer's facilities served at 69 kV or above within a 10-mile radius; data center customers served from lines of 69,000 volts or higher that commenced service on or after 1 October 2025 (a single facility of 50 to 75 MW causing no transmission network upgrade costs may be moved to Rate LP-5 by Commission petition)

cites.quote: have a peak electric demand of 50 MW or greater at a single facility or at least equal to 75 MW in the aggregate among facilities taking service from PPL Electric at or above 69 kV within a 10-mile radius

the customer's interconnection and service requirements do not cause PPL Electric to incur transmission network upgrade costs, then PPL Electric may file a petition with the Commission requesting, subject to Commission review and approval, that the customer's facility be classified under Rate LP-5

min_demand.value: Until the Rate Base Security Obligation is satisfied: the greater of actual peak demand or 80 percent of the load in the load ramp schedule. After it is satisfied: the greater of actual peak demand or 80 percent of the ramp schedule load for the first 5 years of the initial term and 50 percent for the second 5 years. Voluntary interruptible option: minimum load guarantee reduced to 60 percent (first 5 years) and 30 percent (second 5 years). Monthly minimum distribution charge: the Customer Charge of $999.11 per month

cites.quote: (7) Until the LP-6 customer's Rate Base Security Obligation is satisfied, the ESA will require the customer to pay applicable rates based on the greater of actual peak demand values, or 80% of the load provided in the load ramp schedule;

(8) After the LP-6 customer's Rate Base Security Obligation is satisfied, the ESA will require the customer to pay applicable rate based on the greater of actual peak demand values, or 80% of the load provided in the load ramp schedule for the first (5) years of the initial term and 50% for the second five (5) years of the initial term;
If voluntary interruptible service is chosen by the customer, the minimum load guarantee in the customer's ESA would be reduced to 60% for the first five years and 30% for the second five years.
$999.11 per month (Customer Charge)
MINIMUM CHARGE The Monthly Minimum Distribution Charge is the Customer Charge.

contract_term.value: Electric Service Agreement with an initial term of not less than 10 years; initial load ramp schedule for up to the first 5 years of the initial term

cites.quote: (1) The ESA will contain an initial term of not less than ten (10) years; (2) The ESA will require the customer to provide an initial load ramp schedule for up to the first five (5) years of the initial term

collateral.value: Security equal to the cost of the upgrades needed to serve the customer that are placed in rate base and recovered through transmission rates (the Rate Base Security Obligation), by letter of credit, parent guarantee or other instrument acceptable to the Company; satisfied when transmission revenue from the customer equals that obligation. Contribution in aid of construction as up-front milestone payments for directly assignable transmission and distribution upgrades

cites.quote: (3) The ESA will require the LP-6 customer to provide security in an amount equal to the cost of upgrades needed to serve the customer
that are placed into rate base and recovered through transmission rates (such amount is referred to as the "Rate Base Security Obligation")

(4) The ESA will require the security to be provided in the form of a letter of credit, parent guarantee, or other security instrument acceptable to the Company for the amount of the outstanding revenue guarantee;
(6) The ESA will specify that the revenue guarantee shall be satisfied when the Company has received transmission revenue from the customer equaling the Rate Base Security Obligation;
The ESA will require a contribution in aid of construction ("CIAC") as up- front milestone payments ahead of work performed for the cost of directly assignable transmission and distribution upgrades

exit_fee.value: The greater of the remaining minimum load guarantee obligation during the ESA term at termination, or the remaining amount of the Rate Base Security Obligation

cites.quote: (9) The ESA will contain an exit fee that is equal to the remaining minimum load guarantee obligation during the ESA term at the time the customer terminates the ESA, or the remaining amount of the Rate Base Security Obligation, whichever is greater;

rows.license_basis: the PA PUC's docket copy of PPL's filed compliance tariff (www.puc.pa.gov, robots allow it, a public record) and the Commission's letter; the pipeline figure from PPL Corporation's Form 8-K exhibit on SEC EDGAR
rows.erw_overlap: none held for PPL. Window A's large_load_connection_rules/pa_puc_large_load_model_tariff.yaml is the PUC's model, not PPL's tariff, and LP-6 differs from it: threshold 50 MW single or 75 MW aggregate within 10 miles at 69 kV or above (model: 50 MW individually or 100 MW aggregate); initial term at least 10 years with a ramp of up to 5 years (model: at least 5 years after a 3 to 5 year ramp)
rows.notes: LP-6 came out of PPL's base rate case settlement (Joint Petition for Non-Unanimous Settlement filed 13 March 2026, Large Load Interconnections at Joint Petition paragraphs III.I.91 to 97, per the I&E statement in support, www.puc.pa.gov/pcdocs/1918891.pdf p.13), approved as modified by the Opinion and Order entered 11 June 2026; compliance tariff filed 30 June 2026, effective 1 July 2026; replacement pages correcting typographical errors filed 27 August 2026 (the copy read). LP-6 also requires annual load forecasts to the Commission broken down by ESAs, LOAs and inquiries (p.246, Load Forecasts). Beginning 1 January 2027, $11 million a year of Universal Service Rider costs is allocated to LP-6 through a non-bypassable customer charge (pcdocs/1946790.pdf p.56). Pending, a lead not read: the Office of Consumer Advocate's complaint against PPL over data center cost allocation, Docket C-2026-3065756, filed 2 October 2026 per Governor Shapiro's petition to intervene of 15 October 2026 (pa.gov); it seeks a separate data center class and interruptible service, so LP-6 may change. PPL has not filed a tariff on the PUC's model (M-2025-3054271) that I found; the model order sets no filing date for the EDCs (pcdocs/1929842.pdf pp. 117 to 118, ordering paragraphs). PPL's own site (pplelectric.com) bars automated access in its terms of use, so its LP-6 PDF was not read.

rows.license_basis: the Maryland Register as the Division of State Documents publishes it (dsd.maryland.gov, robots allow it) and the session law on the General Assembly's site (mgaleg.maryland.gov, no robots file)
rows.notes: A statewide rule, like window A's Pennsylvania model: it binds each Maryland electric company's own large load tariff. Status: published as proposed on 26 June 2026 with comments to 27 July 2026; whether the PSC has since adopted it was not verified (a later Maryland Register issue would show the final action). Each investor-owned company had to file its own large load rate schedule by 1 September 2026: Chapter 353 (HB 1532, signed 12 May 2026), Public Utilities 4-212(c)(1)(i), p.34 of the session law: 'On or before September 1, 2026, each investor-owned electric company and each electric cooperative shall submit to the Commission for approval a specific rate schedule for large load customers'. BGE's, Pepco's and Delmarva's filings were not read: the PSC's docket system (webpscxb.psc.state.md.us) bars Claude's agents in its robots file (refused). A lead: HB 1082 of 2026 would have moved that date to 1 January 2027 (its fiscal note); Chapter 353 as enacted keeps 1 September 2026. Exelon's Q3 2026 earnings slides (SEC EDGAR, exc-20261030ex992.htm, p.1) give a combined MidAtlantic figure: 'MidAtlantic ~2 GW' of high probability load and 'MidAtlantic ~9 GW' within cluster studies (MidAtlantic covers PECO, BGE, Pepco, Delmarva and Atlantic City Electric). Status updated by the 90-day pass (east-02): was 'proposed' (2026-06-26); The adopted COMAR 20.96.01 took effect on 28 September 2026, the effective date printed in the notice of final action.
